\subsubsection{Approach 1: Direct Correlation}

\textbf{Fitting uncertainty}

Parameter estimates: each entry shows the estimate \(\pm\) the half-width of an approximate 95\% confidence interval. These intervals describe individual fitted coefficients and use the fitted covariance, standard errors, and residual degrees of freedom.

Plotted uncertainty: shading and error bars show approximate 95\% parameter-uncertainty intervals: uncertainty in fitted or calculated values because the model parameters were estimated from data. The selected model, preprocessing, and supplied prediction times and responses are treated as fixed.

The app samples 1,000 sets of parameter values from the fitted multivariate normal covariance approximation (seed 12345), keeping parameter correlations within each fit; separate fits are sampled independently. Bounds enclose the middle 95\% of calculated values at each plotted position (the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles). They do not describe the whole curve simultaneously. Central values use the fitted parameters.

No additional residual or observation noise is added. These are not observation prediction bands: they exclude the additional scatter of future observations, uncertainty about which model to use, and errors from an unsuitable model. Calibration variability still affects the fitted covariance. If sampling fails or a sampled calculation is invalid at a point, its interval is unavailable. A missing interval does not mean zero uncertainty. CV fit variability is a separate descriptive diagnostic.

\textbf{Prediction uncertainty}

Plotted uncertainty: shading and error bars show approximate 95\% parameter-uncertainty intervals: uncertainty in fitted or calculated values because the model parameters were estimated from data. The selected model, preprocessing, and supplied prediction times and responses are treated as fixed.

The app samples 1,000 sets of parameter values from the fitted multivariate normal covariance approximation (seed 12345), keeping parameter correlations within each fit; separate fits are sampled independently. Bounds enclose the middle 95\% of calculated values at each plotted position (the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles). They do not describe the whole curve simultaneously. Central values use the fitted parameters.

No additional residual or observation noise is added. These are not observation prediction bands: they exclude the additional scatter of future observations, uncertainty about which model to use, and errors from an unsuitable model. Calibration variability still affects the fitted covariance. If sampling fails or a sampled calculation is invalid at a point, its interval is unavailable. A missing interval does not mean zero uncertainty. CV fit variability is a separate descriptive diagnostic.

Time mapping: the fitted time relationship is evaluated at each fixed supplied in vitro time for every set of sampled parameters. Horizontal intervals show uncertainty in the mapped in vivo time. Input or mapped times outside the paired-time fitting ranges carry an extrapolation caution.

\subsubsection{Approach 2: Independent Model Fitting}

\textbf{Fitting uncertainty}

Supplied measurement uncertainty: Approach 2 can use an absolute standard deviation (SD) for individual observations or standard error of the mean (SEM) for reported means, entered as a constant or a named column. Replicate counts are optional metadata; the app uses SEM directly without dividing it again. Smaller supplied errors give an observation more influence in fitting. Each calibration source uses its own supplied errors; a source without errors uses residual variation to estimate the uncertainty scale.

Parameter estimates: each entry shows the estimate \(\pm\) the half-width of an approximate 95\% confidence interval for an individual coefficient. With supplied errors, the interval uses the fitted covariance and a normal multiplier, treating those errors as known. Without supplied errors, the interval uses residual variation and, when available, residual degrees of freedom.

Fitting plots: observed-data bars show \(\pm\) one supplied SD or SEM. Shading separately shows approximate pointwise 95\% parameter uncertainty in the fitted curve. The app samples 1,000 complete parameter vectors from the fitted multivariate normal covariance approximation (seed 12345), preserving correlations within each fit. Bounds enclose the middle 95\% of calculated values at each position; they do not describe the whole curve simultaneously.

Time constants: tau summarizes the fitted curve's overall time scale and is evaluated at the fitted parameters by numerical integration. Its table interval is a symmetric approximation based on 50 parameter draws (seed 12345); it is unavailable if sampling or any sampled integration fails. Prediction time intervals separately propagate both calibration fits through the time-constant ratio.

Original measurement errors are assumed independent across rows and times. Time coordinates, the selected model, and normalization constants are held fixed. Fitted-curve intervals exclude future in vivo measurement variability, uncertainty about model choice, and model inadequacy. A missing interval does not mean zero uncertainty. CV fit variability is a separate sensitivity diagnostic.

\textbf{Prediction uncertainty}

Prediction intervals: Approach 2 propagates fitted calibration-parameter uncertainty and, when supplied, uncertainty in the prediction responses. Without supplied prediction uncertainty, those responses are held fixed. Time coordinates, the selected model, and normalization constants are held fixed in either case. Prediction measurements are assumed independent of calibration measurements.

The app samples complete parameter vectors, preserving correlations within each fit and sampling separate calibration fits independently. Prediction draw counts and seeds are method-specific and recorded with the calculated results. Supplied input-response errors are modeled as independent normal errors across entered rows. Centers use the entered responses and fitted parameters. Monte Carlo bounds enclose the middle 95\% of calculated values at each position. Time and response bounds are separate marginal intervals; together they do not form a joint 95\% region or a simultaneous band.

Response-value ratio: the prediction time locates both fitted calibration curves, and their in vivo/in vitro response ratio scales the supplied prediction response. The vertical interval combines calibration-parameter uncertainty with supplied prediction-response uncertainty. Near a zero fitted in vitro response, the ratio can become unstable; the interval is unavailable if the sampled denominator interval includes zero, and a zero or nonfinite fitted denominator also makes the point unavailable.

Time-constant ratio: both time constants are calculated for each sampled pair of calibration parameter sets, and their ratio scales the prediction time. Horizontal time intervals use calibration uncertainty. Supplied prediction-response uncertainty is shown vertically and does not change the mapped time or its interval. Failed sampled integrations make the time interval unavailable without removing a valid point. This overall time scaling can miss differences in curve shape and depends on fitted behavior beyond the observed times.

Observed-response inverse: the fitted in vivo curve is inverted at the supplied prediction response to estimate an in vivo time. Horizontal time intervals combine in vivo calibration uncertainty with supplied prediction-response uncertainty, retaining the dependence between each sampled response and mapped time. The prediction time and fitted in vitro calibration curve are not used to calculate that time. Without future measurement variability, the vertical interval shows supplied prediction-response uncertainty. The search can extend beyond calibration; a prediction is unavailable when a unique time cannot be calculated reliably, for example on a flat part of the curve. By default, a time interval can use successful mappings when the configured minimum fraction of requested draws succeeds at that point. If any draws are excluded, the interval is labeled conditional: its bounds enclose the middle 95\% of successful mappings, not all requested outcomes. Counts, the configured threshold, and failure reasons are retained.

Future in vivo measurements (optional): choose a constant SD/SEM, reuse comparable prediction-input precision, or reuse calibration in vivo precision at the nearest nominal predicted time. Constant values use original in vivo calibration response units and are normalized once; reused values are already on the analyzed scale and retain the source's individual/mean interpretation. Calibration lookup uses analyzed times and extends endpoint errors beyond calibration. Vertical bounds then combine propagated uncertainty and independent normal future measurement errors for one future observation or mean; horizontal time intervals remain unchanged. Inverse future-response bounds use the same successful mappings and conditional rule as the time bounds.

Without the future-measurement option, intervals exclude future in vivo measurement variability. All modes exclude added residual scatter, uncertainty about model choice, and model inadequacy. A finite or narrow interval does not establish that extrapolation is reliable. Outside the conditional inverse rule, failed requested calculations make the affected interval unavailable; a missing interval does not mean zero uncertainty. Intervals that exclude the central estimate are drawn separately at their calculated endpoints. Downloads and reports retain the same bounds and calculation-status details.

\subsubsection{Approach 3: Direct Mapping}

\textbf{Fitting uncertainty}

Parameter uncertainty: Approach 3 does not fit a parametric model, so there is no fitted-parameter covariance matrix, no parameter confidence intervals, and no parameter-uncertainty band.

Fitting plots: the plots show interpolation-based ratios/mappings calculated from the preprocessed datasets. They represent deterministic mappings from the supplied data and preprocessing choices, not statistical uncertainty bands.

\textbf{Prediction uncertainty}

Prediction plot error bars: Approach 3 does not generate formal propagated error bars for prediction outputs because no parametric covariance model is fitted.

The app does not quantify how uncertainty in the input data, preprocessing, or mapping assumptions affects these predictions. Missing error bars do not mean the predictions are exact. Lookup ratios outside the interpolation range remain unavailable rather than extrapolated. A supported mapping that produces a time outside observed calibration is flagged.
